pascals-triangle.d: Return the first numRows rows of Pascal's triangle.
pascals-triangle.i: Each inner entry is the sum of the two above it: row[j] = prev[j-1] + prev[j]. Alternatively build each row directly with C(r, j) = C(r, j-1) * (r - j) / j.
k: Each row from the binomial-coefficient formula

path-crossing.d: Walk a path of N/S/E/W unit moves from the origin. Return true if you ever revisit a point.
path-crossing.i: Track visited coordinates in a HashSet. The key must be value-based: a record, a "x,y" string, or a class overriding equals/hashCode.

permutation-in-string.d: Does s2 contain some permutation of s1 as a substring?
permutation-in-string.i: Fixed-size sliding window of length |s1| with 26-letter counts. Track 'matches' (how many of the 26 counts are equal) so each slide is O(1); found when matches == 26.
k: Fixed window, compare 26 counts each slide

permutations.d: Return all permutations of distinct integers.
permutations.i: Backtracking: at each level pick any unused number (a boolean[] or set of used values), recurse, then un-pick it. Alternative: swap nums[i] into position start.
k: Backtracking with LinkedHashSet of used values

plus-one.d: Add one to a big integer stored as an array of digits.
plus-one.i: From the right: if a digit is < 9, increment it and return. Otherwise set it to 0 and continue. If every digit was 9, return a new array [1, 0, ..., 0].
k: In-place from the right, early return
General carry propagation into a deque

populating-next-right-pointers-in-each-n.d: In a perfect binary tree, set every node's next pointer to the node on its right in the same level (null at the end of a level).
populating-next-right-pointers-in-each-n.i: BFS by levels works with O(n) space. O(1) space: use the next pointers already set on the level above: left.next = right, and right.next = node.next.left.

power-of-three.d: Return whether n is a power of three.
power-of-three.i: Divide by 3 while divisible and check whether you reach 1. No-loop trick: 3^19 (1162261467) is the largest power of 3 in an int, so n > 0 && 1162261467 % n == 0.

product-of-array-except-self.d: Return an array where each position holds the product of all other elements, in O(n) without division.
product-of-array-except-self.i: answer[i] = (product of everything left of i) * (product of everything right of i). Fill prefix products into the output, then multiply in a running suffix product from the right: O(1) extra space.

product-sales-analysis-i.d: For each sale, report the product name, year and price.
product-sales-analysis-i.ex: join Sales with Product on product_id
product-sales-analysis-i.i: INNER JOIN Sales and Product on product_id, then select the needed columns.

rearrange-array-elements-by-sign.d: An array has equally many positives and negatives. Rearrange it to alternate positive, negative, ..., starting with a positive, keeping relative order within each sign.
rearrange-array-elements-by-sign.i: Two write pointers into a new array: positives go to even indices (0, 2, ...), negatives to odd (1, 3, ...).
k: Split into two lists, then interleave

recyclable-and-low-fat-products.d: Return ids of products that are both low fat and recyclable.

redundant-connection.d: A tree with one extra edge added is given as an edge list. Return the edge whose removal restores a tree (the last such edge in the input).
redundant-connection.i: Union-find: process edges in order. The first edge whose endpoints already share a root closes a cycle, so it's the redundant one.

remove-duplicates-from-sorted-array.d: Remove duplicates in place from a sorted array; return the count k of unique values, which must occupy the first k slots.
remove-duplicates-from-sorted-array.i: Slow pointer i marks the last unique value; fast pointer j scans. When nums[j] != nums[i], write it to ++i.

remove-element.d: Remove every occurrence of val in place and return how many elements remain; they must occupy the first k slots (any order).
remove-element.i: Write pointer k: for each element != val, copy it to nums[k++]. Return k.

remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.d: Remove the nth node from the end of a linked list.
remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list.i: One pass: move a fast pointer n steps ahead, then move fast and slow together until fast reaches the last node; slow is just before the target. A dummy head handles removing the first node cleanly.
k: Count length, then walk to L - n

reorder-list.d: Reorder L0 -> L1 -> ... -> Ln into L0 -> Ln -> L1 -> Ln-1 -> ... in place.
reorder-list.i: Three classic steps: find the middle (slow/fast), reverse the second half, then merge the two halves alternately.
k: Nodes in an array + two pointers

replace-employee-id-with-the-unique-iden.d: Show each employee's unique_id (NULL if missing) and name.
replace-employee-id-with-the-unique-iden.ex: Alice has no unique id -> (NULL, Alice)
replace-employee-id-with-the-unique-iden.i: LEFT JOIN keeps every employee even when there's no matching EmployeeUNI row.

reverse-bits.d: Reverse the bits of a 32-bit integer.
reverse-bits.i: 32 times: result = (result << 1) | (n & 1); n >>>= 1. Use the unsigned shift >>> in Java.
k: Shift result left, take n's lowest bit

reverse-integer.d: Reverse the digits of a 32-bit signed integer; return 0 if the result overflows (64-bit integers aren't allowed).
reverse-integer.i: Pop digits with % 10 and push with result*10 + digit. Before pushing, check result against MAX/10 and MIN/10 to detect overflow without using long.
k: Use long and check the range (breaks the no-64-bit rule)

reverse-linked-list.i: Iterative three-pointer pattern: save next, point curr.next to prev, advance prev and curr. Recursive: reverse the rest, then head.next.next = head; head.next = null.
